What is an LLM? · Definitions
AI, machine learning, LLM: what is the difference?
Artificial Intelligence
Machine Learning
Deep Learning
Generative AI
LLMs
ChatGPT · Claude · Gemini
Artificial Intelligence
Computers doing jobs that normally need a human brain.
Machine Learning
Computers that learn from examples, not rules. Like spotting cracks after seeing thousands of photos.
Deep Learning
A powerful kind of machine learning built from layers of “digital neurons”.
Generative AI
AI that creates something new: text, pictures, code, even 3D.
Large Language Model
AI that has read a huge library of text and writes by guessing the next word.

What is an LLM? · Key words
Six words you will hear today
Prompt
The instruction you type to the AI. Think of it as a brief you give a junior.
Example: “Summarise this soil report for the client.”
LLM or chatbot
The AI you chat with: ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini. LLM means Large Language Model.
Example: Asking ChatGPT to draft a letter to the municipality.
Context
Everything you give the AI to work from: files, drawings, notes, past emails.
Example: Uploading the client's brief along with your question.
Hallucination
When the AI makes something up and says it confidently.
Example: Quoting an NBC clause that does not exist.
Open-book answer (RAG)
The AI reads your documents first, then answers from them.
Example: “Using only this NBC 105 PDF, answer and give the clause.”
AI agent
An AI that does several steps by itself, like searching, calculating and filling a sheet.
Example: Collecting supplier prices into an Excel table.

What is an LLM? · How it works
Think of AI as a very fast new junior
Imagine a new junior who…
  • has read millions of books and websites
  • writes a full page in seconds
  • has never visited a site in Nepal
  • never says “I don’t know”, and guesses instead
1
You ask
Type your question and attach your files.
2
It writes word by word
Like phone autocomplete: it keeps adding the word that sounds most likely.
3
You check
Just as you would check a junior’s work before it goes out.
AI writes what sounds right, not what is right.

05 / 35
What is an LLM? · Example
Same question, two confident answers
Question typed twice: “Which Nepal National Building Code covers seismic design of buildings?”
Answer 1: correct
“The seismic design code is NBC 105.”
Answer 2: wrong
“The seismic design code is NBC 101.”
Both sound equally sure. The fix: upload the real code and ask it to quote the clause.

What is an LLM? · Simple ideas
Four ideas that explain how AI behaves
01
It predicts; it does not know
The AI puts words together that usually go together. It has no idea if they are true.
For you: Check every number, clause and name.
02
Open book beats memory
Answers are far better when the AI reads your documents first.
For you: Upload the NBC, the brief or the report.
03
Show your working
Asking for step-by-step answers, like a school maths paper, cuts mistakes.
For you: Add “show every step” to calculations.
04
Good at some jobs, bad at similar ones
Great at a letter, then wrong on a table that looks just as easy.
For you: Never assume; check each new kind of task.

What is an LLM? · Strengths
What AI does well, and where it fails
Good at: let it draft
  • Writing and polishing letters, reports and specs
  • Summarising long documents and meetings
  • Turning messy notes into neat tables
  • Suggesting ideas and questions to ask
  • Translating between Nepali and English
  • Writing small computer scripts and Excel formulas
Weak at: you must check
  • Maths and unit conversions (use a calculator)
  • Latest NBC, bylaws and district rates, unless you upload them
  • Giving real sources from memory
  • Understanding drawings accurately
  • Knowing when it is wrong
  • Taking responsibility for a design

Which tools? · By job
Pick the right tool for the job
NotebookLM
Answers only from files you upload, such as NBC or soil reports, and shows where. Still check.
Perplexity
Searches the web and gives links: suppliers, product data, standards.
Projects
In ChatGPT or Claude: keep one project's brief, specs and minutes together.
Offline AI
Ollama or LM Studio run AI on your own PC. Nothing goes online.
Scripts and Excel
Excel formulas, Python, Dynamo and Grasshopper scripts, automation.
Image tools
Mood boards and concept pictures from a description. Ideas, not design.

How to ask well · Process
Six steps to use AI on real work
01
Decide the job
One clear output: a brief, a table, a letter, a checklist.
02
Check your data
Public, internal or private? This decides which tool you may use.
03
Give it material
Attach the brief, drawings, code pages or past examples.
04
Ask clearly
Say who it should act as, the goal, the facts, the steps, the format.
05
Improve the answer
Ask follow-ups: “what did you miss?”, “make it shorter”.
06
Check and own it
Check numbers, clauses and sources. You sign, so you decide.

13 / 35
How to ask well · Good vs bad
Escape the one-line prompt trap
Bad prompt: one line
“Write a commercial building design strategy.”
What happens: a vague, general answer that could be for any city in the world. You keep retrying and wasting time.
It is like telling a new junior engineer “do the building” and walking away.
Good prompt: a proper briefing
“Act as an architectural consultant. I am planning a 6-storey commercial building on a 10-aana plot in Kathmandu. Suggest a design strategy for shops, offices and parking. Consider seismic safety, municipal bylaws and monsoon drainage. Give a table, and list your assumptions.”
What happens: a focused, local, usable first draft on the first try.

How to ask well · Recipe
The six parts of a good prompt
[ROLE] Act as an architectural assistant for a design firm in Kathmandu.
[GOAL] Turn the attached client email into a clear design brief.
[CONTEXT] Residential duplex in Jhamsikhel, Lalitpur; plot [__] aana; family of [__]; budget about NPR [__] lakh; Lalitpur Metropolitan City bylaws apply.
[ACTION] 1) List what the client wants. 2) Mark what is fact and what is your guess. 3) List what is missing.
[OUTPUT] A table: need | words from the email | fact or guess. Then up to 10 questions for the client.
[LIMITS] Do not invent sizes or bylaw figures. If something is not stated, write “not stated”.
ROLE
Who should the AI pretend to be?
GOAL
What exactly do you want back?
CONTEXT
Project facts and local rules
ACTION
The steps, in order
OUTPUT
The shape of the answer: table, list, letter
LIMITS
What it must not do

How to ask well · Techniques
Four basic ways to ask
Just ask (zero-shot)
Ask directly, with no examples.
“Summarise this soil test report in five points for the client.”
Show examples (few-shot)
Paste one to three samples of what you want.
Paste two old RFIs, then: “Write the next RFI in the same style.”
Give it a role
Tell it which professional to act as, and for whom.
“Act as a quantity surveyor in Nepal, explaining to a first-time house builder.”
Show your working
Ask it to go step by step, like a maths exam.
“Show every step with units before giving the final number.”
Square Unit CPD · LLMs for Architecture & Engineering
16 / 35
How to ask well · Checking
Always check the AI's maths: an example
Question: 45 m³ of M20 concrete, mix 1:1.5:3. How many cement bags, and how much sand and aggregate?
Item
Hand check
Result
Dry volume
45 m³ × 1.54
69.30 m³
Cement
69.30 ÷ 5.5 × 1440 kg ÷ 50 kg
≈ 363 bags
Sand
12.60 m³ × 1.5 × 35.31
≈ 667 cft
Aggregate
12.60 m³ × 3 × 35.31
≈ 1,335 cft
If the AI’s answer is different, find out why before it goes to a client or supplier.
Questions to ask
  • Dry volume factor 1.54 used?
  • Cement 1440 kg/m³, 50 kg bags?
  • Nominal mix OK, or design mix needed?
  • Wastage (2–5%) added or not?

How to ask well · Safety habits
Six habits to avoid AI mistakes
Ask for the source
Clause number, page or link. Then open it and read it yourself.
Let it say “I don't know”
Tell it to write “not stated” instead of guessing.
Give it the real document
Upload the actual NBC, report or drawing. Don't trust its memory.
Use a calculator
Check numbers in Excel or by hand, never trust chat maths alone.
Protect client data
No citizenship copies, lalpurja or private client files in free tools.
Keep a record
Note the tool, date, what was checked and by whom.

The legal side · Principles
Four legal rules, in plain words
01
You are responsible
AI cannot hold a licence. The engineer or architect who signs and stamps is fully responsible.
02
Check like a professional
Using unchecked AI answers for structure or code can be treated as negligence.
03
Keep secrets secret
Uploading client files to public tools may break confidentiality. AI-only work has weak copyright.
04
People approve, not AI
NBC and bylaw compliance is certified by people. AI is only an unlicensed helper.

19 / 35
The legal side · Real cases
What courts and governments have already said
Fake court cases
USA · Mata v. Avianca · 2023
Lawyers were fined US$5,000 for submitting court cases ChatGPT had invented.
Lesson: Submitting unchecked AI work is your mistake, not the software's.
Who owns AI work?
US Copyright Office · 2025
Typing a prompt alone does not make you the author. Your own changes and choices can be protected.
Lesson: Keep a record of your own design input.
Europe's AI law
EU AI Act · in force Aug 2024
Rules based on risk, with transparency duties for AI makers.
Lesson: Foreign clients may ask how you use AI.

The legal side · Nepal
What Nepali law and policy say
Law or policy
What it means for you
National AI Policy 2082 (Aug 2025)
A government policy, not yet a law. Plans an AI regulator, a National AI Centre, data-protection laws and rules against misuse.
Nepal Engineering Council Act 2055
Only registered engineers may practise. The registered person, not the tool, is answerable.
Individual Privacy Act 2075
Clients' personal data needs consent and protection. Think before uploading.
Copyright Act 2059
Protects the work of human creators, including architectural works. AI-only work is unclear.
Electronic Transactions Act 2063
Covers e-records and e-signatures, and crimes like accessing data without permission.
NBC, bylaws and naksa pass
Approval is given by people and the municipality. AI summaries help; they never approve.
For awareness only; not legal advice. Confirm details with a lawyer or the Nepal Engineering Council.

You check

  • The actual NBC clause
  • Site and client facts

Engineer decides
  • Design choices
  • Code compliance and safety
  • Advice to the client
  • The signature and stamp

Use case 01
Client Brief Extraction
The task
Turn a long, messy client email into a clear list of what they want.
Nepal scenario
A family emails a rambling 4-page note, half Nepali and half English, for a duplex in Jhamsikhel: rooms, a puja room, parking, a rental flat and a budget.
Bad prompt
“Design this building for the client.”
Why it fails: AI cannot design from one vague line. You get a generic house with no link to the client.
Good prompt (copy this)
“Act as an architectural programming assistant. Analyze this client brief and extract functional, spatial and environmental requirements. Separate facts from assumptions. List missing information and questions for the client.”
What you get
A tidy list of needs, facts vs guesses, and questions to ask.
Check before use
Every item must trace back to the client's own words.
Practise this: AI Prompt Manual, page 4
23 / 35
Use case 02
Space Programming (100-Room Hotel)
The task
Work out the rooms, areas and what sits next to what, before drawing plans.
Nepal scenario
A boutique resort in Pokhara near Phewa Lake. The owner wants the right balance of guest areas and back-of-house (kitchen, laundry, staff).
Bad prompt
“Design a 100-room hotel.”
Why it fails: Far too big an ask. You get a random room list with no reasoning.
Good prompt (copy this)
“I'm designing a 100-room hotel. Develop a space-programming framework covering guest areas, BOH, service and accessibility. For each space, identify function, users, adjacencies and open questions.”
What you get
A room-by-room table with users, neighbours and open questions.
Check before use
Compare areas with Department of Tourism hotel standards and past projects.
Practise this: AI Prompt Manual, page 6
24 / 35
Use case 03
Research Framework (Sustainable Office)
The task
Plan what to study for a greener, cooler building, and how to measure it.
Nepal scenario
A mid-rise office in Kathmandu: sunny winters, heavy monsoon, dust. The client wants less air-conditioning and more daylight.
Bad prompt
“Tell me about sustainable buildings.”
Why it fails: You get a textbook essay, mostly about other climates.
Good prompt (copy this)
“I am designing a mid-rise office building in Kathmandu. Create a research framework covering orientation, daylighting, ventilation and envelope. For each topic, give the research question, data required and a metric to verify.”
What you get
A research plan: question, data needed, how to measure success.
Check before use
Use real local weather data (DHM) and check every metric.
Practise this: AI Prompt Manual, page 8
25 / 35
Use case 04
Meeting Minutes to Action Tracker
The task
Turn scribbled meeting notes into who-does-what-by-when.
Nepal scenario
A coordination meeting of architect, structural, MEP consultants and contractor. Notes were jotted in mixed Nepali and English.
Bad prompt
“Summarize the meeting.”
Why it fails: A vague paragraph with no names, no deadlines, no follow-up.
Good prompt (copy this)
“Convert these meeting notes into structured minutes: decisions made, issues raised, responsibilities, deadlines and pending items. Do not invent information that wasn't discussed.”
What you get
A clean action table you can email the same day.
Check before use
Send it to attendees to confirm before it becomes the record.
Practise this: AI Prompt Manual, page 10
26 / 35
Use case 05
Preliminary Cost Estimation Framework
The task
Break an early budget into big cost headings and spot the risks.
Nepal scenario
A mixed-use building in Kathmandu, shops below and flats above. The client asks for a rough budget in NPR before any drawings.
Bad prompt
“What will this building cost?”
Why it fails: It invents a number in dollars with no basis. Dangerous if shown to a client.
Good prompt (copy this)
“Break this brief into major cost categories, flag items needing QS confirmation, and list your rate assumptions. Don't present this as a final price. Use NPR.”
What you get
Cost headings, assumed rates and a list of items to confirm.
Check before use
Use current district rates and get a quantity surveyor to confirm.
Practise this: AI Prompt Manual, page 12
27 / 35
Use case 06
NBC Code Compliance Querying
The task
Find the relevant NBC requirements quickly, from the actual code.
Nepal scenario
Checking earthquake-resistant (ductile) detailing for a 4-storey RC house in Kathmandu Valley before submitting for naksa pass.
Bad prompt
“Is my building code compliant?”
Why it fails: AI cannot see your building, and may quote clauses from memory that do not exist.
Good prompt (copy this)
“Based on the uploaded NBC 105 (Seismic Design of Buildings in Nepal) document, what are the specific structural limitations and ductility requirements for a 4-storey residential building located in Kathmandu Valley? Cite the specific sections.”
What you get
A list of requirements, each with its clause number.
Check before use
Open every cited clause. The structural engineer signs off, not AI.
Practise this: AI Prompt Manual, page 14
28 / 35
Use case 07
Quantity Surveying & Material Ratios
The task
Work out cement bags, sand and aggregate from a concrete volume.
Nepal scenario
Footings for a house: the contractor needs to order cement, sand and gitti from a local supplier this week.
Bad prompt
“How much concrete materials do I need?”
Why it fails: No volume, grade or mix given, so any number it gives is a guess.
Good prompt (copy this)
“Act as an expert quantity surveyor in Nepal. I have a concrete volume of 45 cubic metres for M20 grade concrete. Using a nominal mix ratio of 1:1.5:3, calculate the exact bags of cement, volume of sand (cft) and volume of aggregate needed. Show every step. Format the output as a clean table for a client proposal.”
What you get
A step-by-step table: about 363 bags, 667 cft sand, 1,335 cft aggregate.
Check before use
Recheck by hand (see the checking slide) and add wastage.
Practise this: AI Prompt Manual, page 16
29 / 35
Use case 08
Rapid Concept Render Prompting
The task
Write a clear description for an AI image tool to make mood-board pictures.
Nepal scenario
A contemporary house in Patan, Lalitpur, that respects the traditional Newari brick look of the neighbourhood.
Bad prompt
“Make a cool house render.”
Why it fails: You get a generic Western villa that has nothing to do with Nepal.
Good prompt (copy this)
“A photorealistic render of a modern 3-storey house in Lalitpur, Nepal. Traditional Newari brickwork (Maapaa) on the ground floor, paired with minimalist glass and exposed concrete above. Midday clear sky, lush local courtyard vegetation.”
What you get
Mood-board pictures to discuss style with the client.
Check before use
Pictures are ideas, not buildable designs. Heritage bylaws still apply.
Practise this: AI Prompt Manual, page 18
30 / 35
Use case 09
Site Coordination & Voice Notes
The task
Turn voice notes from a site walk into an issues list and RFIs.
Nepal scenario
A site engineer walks a multi-storey site in Balkhu, recording notes in Nepali about honeycombing in columns and misaligned rebar.
Bad prompt
“Fix the issues mentioned in my site audio recording.”
Why it fails: AI cannot fix a site. It may also invent details that were never said.
Good prompt (copy this)
“Convert this site audio transcript into a structured matrix: 1. Critical Non-Conformances 2. Consultant RFIs 3. Responsible Parties and Deadlines. Do not assume facts not stated.”
What you get
An issues table with RFIs, owners and deadlines.
Check before use
Attach site photos and confirm with the team. Structural defects go to the structural engineer.
Practise this: AI Prompt Manual, page 20

Architecture + AI
